open_points.subject: store.open_store start-up cleanup
open_points.text: “On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names … are removed” contradicts “The store's own temporary files … are removed, and nothing else is.”
open_points.question: Does store.open_store remove unreferenced content-addressed value bytes at start, and if not, which operation does?
options: store.open_store removes temporary files and unreferenced value bytes
store.open_store removes only temporary files and another start-up operation removes unreferenced value bytes
unreferenced value bytes are not removed
open_points.default_guess: Have store.open_store remove both temporary files and unreferenced value bytes, as A18 and the State 4 recovery flow require.

open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list recovery after an invalid configuration
open_points.text: “Re-read when the file's digest changed or it cannot be read” and “a failed re-read leaves no list until one passes” do not say what triggers another read when the file is restored to exactly the bytes of the last valid configuration.
open_points.question: After a failed re-read clears the token list, must every request retry reading until a valid list is obtained, even when the restored file digest equals the last successful digest?
options: Retry on every request while no valid token list exists
Retry only after the file digest differs from the last successfully read digest
Remember the failed file state and retry when that state changes
open_points.default_guess: Retry on every request while the current token list is absent.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes refusal at the MCP boundary
open_points.text: “a text JCS cannot represent is invalid_request” conflicts with “Errors: refused for a value JCS cannot represent” and “surface returns it unchanged except internal_error and stop_required.”
open_points.question: What refusal code does the MCP caller receive when canonicalization rejects a non-finite number or duplicate object key?
options: invalid_request only for surface-originated values and refused for internal callers
open_points.default_guess: Return invalid_request at the MCP boundary and reserve refused for direct internal calls.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input representation
open_points.text: The operation takes “One JSON value” but must reject “a duplicate key,” although duplicate keys are no longer observable after ordinary JSON parsing.
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text or a parsed representation that preserves duplicate object members, and which module detects duplicate keys?
options: canonical_bytes receives raw JSON text and parses it with duplicate detection
surface parses with duplicate detection and canonical_bytes receives an already validated value
canonical_bytes receives a lossless parsed JSON representation retaining duplicate members
open_points.default_guess: Let surface parse with duplicate-key detection before passing a validated JSON value to canonical_bytes.

open_points.subject: functions.add_captured_trial_case file-copy atomicity
open_points.text: “all before any byte is copied — only then each spooled file is copied … so a refusal copies nothing” conflicts with store.put_value_bytes being able to return refused for a digest or size mismatch after an earlier file has already been published.
open_points.question: For a capture containing several files, what happens if validation while copying a later file finds a digest or size mismatch after earlier files were published?
options: Pre-read and verify every source file before publishing any of them
Treat a source-byte mismatch as internal_error, allowing earlier unnamed bytes to remain
Roll back or remove bytes published earlier by the same capture
Return refused even though earlier unnamed bytes remain
open_points.default_guess: Pre-read and verify all source files before publishing any captured fixture.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.prepare_request prepared-request output
open_points.text: The output is “A prepared request” while service_invoker “hides HTTP transport” and “only it holds the credential at the answer”; the text does not say whether the returned object exposes the credential-bearing headers to effects.
open_points.question: Is the prepared request an opaque, single-module-owned value that effects can only pass back to send_prepared_request, or may effects inspect its complete URL, headers and body?
options: Opaque prepared-request handle; only service_invoker can inspect credential-bearing wire data
Structured request visible to effects but with the credential value stored separately inside service_invoker
Complete request, including credential value, returned to effects
open_points.default_guess: Use an opaque prepared-request value and return the separate credential-free description and digest for effects to inspect.
